title: SLI aggregation strategy and dashboard pruning notes
summary: Working notes for establishing consistent SLI aggregation rules, histogram bucket guidelines, trace span naming conventions, and a pragmatic dashboard pruning schedule for the observability org.
body:
Context and motivation:
- We're accumulating many model- and route-specific dashboards; some have overlapping metrics and unclear owners. This doc proposes a lightweight SLI aggregation model and a dashboard lifecycle to reduce noise and ensure SLOs remain actionable.

Goals (concise):
- Define canonical aggregation rules for counters/gauges/histograms for token-serving workloads.
- Provide recommended latency bucket boundaries for model inference histograms.
- Standardize tracing span names and minimal trace anchors for cross-service joins.
- Provide a repeatable dashboard pruning/archival cadence and owner rotation.

1) Metric type rules (how to aggregate)
- Counters (e.g., tokens_generated_total, request_failures_total): sum across instances for global SLI; use rate() or increase() over the SLI window (see below).
- Gauges (e.g., connection_pool_size): report instance-level; do not sum. Use max() for capacity-sensitive SLIs, avg() for utilization SLIs.
- Histograms/summaries (latency): prefer histogram buckets (tdigests/summaries acceptable if supported). For SLOs use histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(req_latency_bucket[window])) by (le)). Avoid naively taking p99 from client-side summaries without alignment.

2) Aggregation windows and alignment (practical defaults)
- Short window SLIs (latency p50/p95/p99): 5m rate with 1m scrape resolution; compute over a rolling 5m to detect regressions without too many false positives.
- Error-rate SLIs: 1m and 1h windows (short alert vs long-term burn). Use ratio of increases: increase(failures_total[window]) / increase(requests_total[window]).
- Throughput (rps/tokens/sec): 5m rate with per-model and per-route breakdown. For cost analysis, compute per-1000-token unit metrics.

3) Histogram bucket suggestions (in ms, model inference end-to-end)
- Extremely low-latency targets (small models / local): [1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024] ms
- General-purpose (production hosted models): [5,10,20,40,80,160,320,640,1280,2560] ms
- Large context / heavy models: [20,50,100,200,400,800,1600,3200,6400] ms
Notes: choose symmetric geometric progression so quantile calculations interpolate well. Align model variants where possible (same bucket set) so dashboards and HPA rules can be compared.

4) Prometheus/Query examples (copy-paste friendly)
- p99 latency (histogram): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(model_infer_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route))
- error rate: sum(increase(route_errors_total{route="/generate"}[5m])) / sum(increase(route_requests_total{route="/generate"}[5m]))
- tokens per second (per model): sum(rate(tokens_generated_total[5m])) by (model)

5) Tracing: minimal conventions to keep traces joinable and low-cardinality
- Span naming: service.operation.resource where resource is coarse (e.g., serving.runtime.generate, storage.kv.get, model.loader.load). Avoid including model_name or request_id in span name.
- Attributes/Tags: attach model_id, model_variant, route (path), and sampling.signal boolean to the root span as attributes. These keys should be stable (model_id consistent across infra).
- Trace anchors (minimal set): the root request span should include request_id and route; the model execute span should propagate model_variant and gpu_node (if applicable). Use these two spans as join anchors between traces and logs/metrics.
- Sampling: keep configurable head-sampling (1-2%) plus error-based sampling for traces with status != OK. Ensure sampled traces include full KV/DB spans when errors occur.

6) Dashboard curation and pruning policy (practical lifecycle)
- Naming + namespace rule: dashboards should be prefixed with team and purpose: observability/<team>/<short-name> or eng/<team>/model-<model>-health.
- Ownership: every dashboard must have an owner (Slack handle and email) in the dashboard metadata. Owners are expected to: review yearly, respond to alerts, and attend pruning reviews.
- Pruning cadence: quarterly sweep by central Observability with team reps. Categories:
  * Active (SLI+alerts configured, owner engaged) -> keep.
  * Dormant (no edits/uses > 180 days but linked to an active SLO) -> archive to read-only folder and notify owner.
  * Orphaned (no owner or no usage > 365 days) -> auto-archive, create ticket to delete.
- Archival storage: snapshot dashboard JSON to a /dashboards/archive/ folder in GitHub along with PR metadata for retrieval.

7) Ownership rotation and runbook tie-ins
- When a dashboard backs an SLO, the oncall rotation for that SLO must include a named dashboard owner. Oncall owners rotate quarterly; central Observability will send a calendar invite to the new owner + team lead.
- Runbook checklist for incident triage: which dashboards to open first (latency heatmap -> per-model histogram -> traces filtered to route). Keep a top-5 quick-links panel on each SLO dashboard.

8) Migration steps for legacy dashboards (actionable)
- Inventory: run current-dashboard-export and tag by metric prefixes (model_infer_*, tokens_*).
- Consolidate candidates: group per-model dashboards that only differ by label filters into a single templated dashboard with model variable.
- Replace and retire: push templated dashboards as PRs, add alias redirects for old links for 90 days, then archive originals.

Open questions / discussion items:
- How aggressive should auto-archival be for short-lived experimentation dashboards created by Solutions Eng? Proposal: 90 days TTL for experiment dashboards unless owner flags them as permanent.
- Do we want a central library of canonical histogram buckets for every model family? Pro: comparability. Con: some models need custom buckets. Suggest starting with 3 canonical families (small/general/large) and iterate.

Immediate next steps (owners assigned):
- Ravi: script inventory export and produce a CSV of dashboards with last_edit, owner, linked_SLO (due 2024-10-01)
- Nina: draft templated dashboard JSON for model family 'general' and put in PR (telemetry repo) by 2024-10-10
- Ava: coordinate quarterly pruning calendar and send invites to product/platform leads by 2024-10-07

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider flagging dashboards that query high-cardinality label sets (e.g., model_id + host + route) and suggest cardinality-reduced views to avoid Prometheus slow queries.
- For tracing, a lightweight span-sampling flag (sampled_for_debug=true) that looks for correlated anomalies across p99 spikes could reduce noise for investigations.

Appendix: quick checklist for dashboard reviewers
- Does it back an SLO? If yes, ensure owner metadata and alert linkage.
- Are histogram bucket sets aligned to canonical family? If not, justify.
- Are queries using rates/increases for counters? Replace instant counters with increase() where appropriate.
- Is the dashboard creating high-cardinality queries? If yes, add template variables or reduce label dims.

End of notes. Feedback welcome — I'll convert to a short playbook page once we converge on defaults.
